drawdown_context: UPBD is the rebranded Rent-A-Center / Acima / Brigit holding company. As of the 2025-05-15 cutoff, the company had just completed the $460M Brigit acquisition (Jan 31, 2025) financed largely by drawing $323M on the ABL revolver, lifting outstanding debt from $1.3B (12/31/24) to $1.5B (3/31/25). Q1 2025 RAC same-store sales turned negative (-2.0%) after a +1.5% FY24 print, but the CFPB voluntarily dismissed (with prejudice) its lawsuit against Acima on March 6, 2025, releasing the $45M acquisition escrow and removing the largest single regulatory overhang. CEO Mitchell Fadel announced retirement effective June 1, 2025 with CFO Fahmi Karam succeeding (already CFO since Oct 2022 - orderly succession).

rfm_tuples.R: 'In May 2023, in accordance with the CFPB NORA process, the CFPB staff notified Acima that the staff may recommend that the CFPB take legal action against Acima... On July 26, 2024, the CFPB filed a lawsuit against Acima and its former founder in the U.S. District Court for the District of Utah... Both lawsuits remain pending... the CFPB initial monetary settlement demand exceeded the remaining $45 million holdback by a substantial amount.' (10-K, Feb 25, 2025)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B claim_evolution: track CFPB litigation status between the FY24 10-K (filed Feb 25, 2025) and the pre-cutoff Q1 2025 10-Q. The 10-K describes the case as a live existential risk; check whether the Q1 disclosure mirrors that framing or has materially changed.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025 10-Q (period ending Mar 31, 2025) confirms: 'On March 6, 2025, the CFPB voluntarily dismissed with prejudice its lawsuit against Acima... Acima did not pay any money, was not required to change any business practices, nor was it subject to any injunctive or other relief... As a result of the CFPB dismissal of its lawsuit against Acima, the full amount of the escrow was released to the former owners of Acima as provided by the merger agreement.' This occurred 9 days AFTER the 10-K was signed (Feb 25). The 10-K disclosed the worst case while the Q1 10-Q disclosed full vindication.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: This is a Mode-B WIN, not a red flag. Management disclosed the CFPB risk honestly in the 10-K (with full quantification of the holdback shortfall risk and explicit acknowledgment of a settlement demand exceeding $45M); 9 days later the regulator capitulated entirely under the new CFPB administration's enforcement pullback. The honesty-alpha framework correctly flags this as conservative-disclosure, not lying-by-omission. Materially de-risks the largest single overhang on the equity.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 RAC segment: 'Change in same store sales 1.5%' (10-K, Segment Performance) vs Q1 2025 10-Q segment table: 'Revenues $489,025 ... Change in same store sales (2.0)% Stores in same store sales calculation 1,564 ... due to a decrease in same store sales of 2.0%, driven by an decrease in rentals and fees revenues of $24.6 million resulting from tightening of underwriting and removing certain products from our lineup to protect our LCO rate.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B claim_evolution: detect inflection in the core RAC franchise. FY24 +1.5% same-store turning to -2.0% in Q1 2025 = 350bps deterioration on the legacy subprime household consumer.
rfm_tuples.M_source: claim_evolution (10-K Item 7 vs 10-Q MD&A) - direct segment-table comparison
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24 RAC SSS: +1.5% on 1,578 stores. Q1 2025 RAC SSS: -2.0% on 1,564 stores. Lease portfolio value declined to $129.9M (Q1 2025) from $136.8M (FY24-end), a 5.0% sequential drop. Same-store lease portfolio value at $117.4M Q1 vs $123.4M FY24-end (-4.9% sequential). Operating profit dropped from $78.1M (Q1 2024) to $66.4M (Q1 2025), down 15%. Management attributes the SSS decline to underwriting tightening and product mix removal 'to protect our LCO rate' - a defensive posture indicating subprime customer stress.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Classic claim drift: the FY24 10-K framed RAC as stable (+1.5% SSS), but Q1 2025 shows a 350bps swing to negative with management explicitly tightening underwriting. This is a leading indicator of subprime household stress that the 10-K narrative did not flag with appropriate emphasis (it was disclosed as a positive metric). The shrinking portfolio value (-5% sequential) and 15% operating profit drop in the legacy cash-cow segment indicate the Acima/Brigit growth narrative is masking core franchise erosion.

rfm_tuples.R: 'On January 31, 2025, we completed the acquisition of Brigit for total consideration of up to $460 million, consisting of approximately $278.7 million in cash consideration and approximately 2.7 million shares of Upbound Group, Inc. common stock at closing, $75 million in deferred consideration, payable in multiple installments, and an earnout of up to $60 million based on the achievement of certain financial performance metrics for the Brigit business in 2026.' (10-K). 'On January 31, 2025, we used $323 million of our available commitments under our ABL Credit Facility to finance the Brigit acquisition.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-A: confirm Brigit acquisition closed and was funded. Mode-B: test whether the ABL draw was disclosed at the time of the 10-K and whether liquidity was materially impaired. Verify post-closing leverage and ABL availability.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K stated post-Brigit (Feb 18, 2025): $113.7M cash, $94.5M ABL availability net of LCs. Q1 2025 10-Q (Mar 31): $107.3M cash, $1.5B total debt (up from $1.3B at 12/31/24), $137.7M operating cash flow Q1 (vs $45.4M Q1 2024, +203% YoY). Brigit Q1 contribution: $31.9M revenue, $8.8M operating profit at 27.7% margin, 1.23M paying users. Brigit purchase price = ~14.4x Q1 annualized operating profit; net advance losses 2.4%. Subsequent April 24 cash on hand $59.3M / ABL availability $134.5M.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Brigit acquisition consummated and segment performance is strong in Q1, but the financing structure is concerning: cash position swung from $60.9M (12/31/24) to $113.7M (post-Brigit Feb 18) back to $59.3M (April 24) - a $54M cash burn in ~2 months suggesting post-acquisition working capital pressure. The $75M deferred consideration + $60M earnout creates additional 2026 cash-call. Operating cash flow trajectory is positive (Q1 jumped to $137.7M), which mitigates this; but the leverage step-up combined with negative RAC SSS warrants moderate concern.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Cash provided by operating activities decreased by $95.6 million to $104.7 million in 2024 from $200.3 million in 2023, primarily due to an increase in our inventory purchases driven by increased consumer demand.' (10-K) 'We believe cash flow generated from operations and availability under our ABL Credit Facility, will be sufficient to fund our operations during the next twelve months.'
rfm_tuples.f: Liquidity bridge: operating cash flow dropped 48% YoY in FY24. Test whether the 'sufficient for next twelve months' framing survives the Brigit $323M ABL draw + $75M deferred consideration + 2026 earnout.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24 OCF $104.7M (vs FY23 $200.3M, -48%). Capital return: $82.3M dividends + $0 buyback = $82.3M (well below FY24 OCF of $104.7M, a CHANGE from prior practice). Note: NO buybacks in 2024 (had $50M FY23, $235M remaining auth as of 12/31/24 - explicit decision to halt). Q1 2025 OCF $137.7M (vs Q1 2024 $45.4M, +203%) - strong rebound. Interest expense run-rate $27.1M Q1 2025 (vs $29.2M Q1 2024) - slight decline despite higher debt due to mix shift to lower-cost ABL.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Management explicitly suspended buybacks in 2024 (zero repurchases vs $50M prior year), preserving cash ahead of the Brigit deal. This is a positive governance signal (capital discipline) NOT a red flag. Q1 OCF rebound to $137.7M (annualizing >$500M) shows the OCF compression was working-capital timing, not structural. Dividend ($82.3M) was well-covered. The 'sufficient for next twelve months' framing is honestly stated.

rfm_tuples.R: 'In October 2020... Acima received a Civil Investigative Demand from the CFPB... In November 2021, Acima received a letter from the Nebraska Attorney General office stating that the Attorney General of Nebraska, along with a coalition of thirty-eight state Attorneys General, initiated a multi-state investigation... In March 2024, the Multistate presented their findings and allegations from their investigation to Acima.' NYAG: 'On August 14, 2024... the NYAG filed a lawsuit against Acima in the Supreme Court of the State of New York'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B regulatory exposure persistence: even after CFPB dismissal (C1), Multistate (40 states + DC) and NYAG litigation remain. Test whether reserves and disclosure are commensurate.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Legal reserves at 12/31/24: $20.7M (vs $8.8M at 12/31/23, +135%). At 3/31/25: still $20.7M (unchanged). Q1 2025 the company recorded $10.0M in additional legal accruals for regulatory matters during the quarter. The 10-K explicitly states 'we are unable to estimate a range of losses related to these matters that may be reasonably possible.' Multistate settlement discussions ongoing; NYAG motion to dismiss pending. Acima held $45M escrow released after CFPB win - none remains for Multistate or NYAG.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Legal reserves more than doubled FY23 to FY24 ($8.8M -> $20.7M), and the company recorded an additional $10M of regulatory accruals in Q1 2025 - a meaningful run-rate. The 40-state Multistate AG matter and NYAG suit remain genuine tail risks even after CFPB dismissal. The 'unable to estimate range of loss' disclosure is honest but means a future $50-200M+ settlement is on the table. With the $45M Acima escrow released back to the former founder post-CFPB dismissal, there is no longer indemnification cushion.

rfm_tuples.R: 'During the year ended December 31, 2024, consolidated revenues and gross profit increased by approximately $328.2 million and $58.1 million, respectively, primarily due to an increase in the Acima segment revenues described below... The Acima segment revenues increased approximately by $330.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, due to increases in rentals and fees revenues and merchandise sales of $244.9 million and $84.1 million, respectively, primarily resulting from an increase in GMV of 17.1%.' (10-K) 'Merchandise losses in our Acima locations due to LCOs, expressed as a percentage of revenues, were approximately 9.4% in 2024, compared to 9.3% in 2023.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B unit-economics test: Acima 17.1% GMV growth is the central growth story. Test if growth is profitable (LCO rate stable) and if Q1 2025 confirms the trajectory.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Acima FY24 segment ops margin 11.3% (vs 12.2% FY23, -90bps); LCOs stable at 9.4%. Q1 2025 Acima: revenue $637.3M vs $561.3M Q1 2024 = +13.5% YoY; operating profit $73.7M vs $51.9M = +42% YoY; operating margin 11.6% (improving). LCO rate 8.9% in Q1 2025 (vs 9.6% Q1 2024) - 70bps improvement. Acima Q1 operating profit beat: continued GMV expansion + lower LCOs.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The Acima growth story has held up cleanly across the FY24 10-K and the Q1 2025 10-Q. GMV growth 17.1% FY24 maintaining mid-teens trajectory; LCOs actually IMPROVING 70bps YoY in Q1 (9.6% -> 8.9%); operating margin expanding 11.3% -> 11.6%. This is the strongest fundamental tell in the filing complex: the growth segment is actually compounding. Honesty-alpha framework: management is delivering on the stated thesis with verifiable Q1 confirmation.

rfm_tuples.R: 'On February 20, 2025, we announced that Mitchell E. Fadel will retire from his position as Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board of Directors, effective June 1, 2025. Fahmi Karam will succeed Mr. Fadel as Chief Executive Officer and a member of the Board of Directors at that time. Mr. Karam has served as Chief Financial Officer since October 2022. On February 18, 2025, Sudeep Gautam, former Executive Vice President Chief Technology and Digital Officer, departed the Company.' (10-K, Item 7)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B insider_vs_calendar: CEO retirement announced 5 days before 10-K filing, with CFO (>2-year tenure) succeeding. CTO departure same week. Test against bad-news disclosure pattern.
rfm_tuples.M_value: CEO Fadel retirement announced Feb 20, 2025; 10-K filed Feb 25, 2025. CFO Karam has 2.5-year tenure (since Oct 2022), succeeding as CEO - orderly internal promotion. CTO Sudeep Gautam departed Feb 18, 2025 (2 days before CEO announcement, 7 days before 10-K). The CEO transition was disclosed in an 8-K Feb 20 and incorporated into the 10-K (which was signed by Karam as CFO). No interim CFO required because Karam continues as CFO until June 1.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Unlike JACK (CFO departed 1 day before 10-K filing), UPBD CEO transition was disclosed 5 days BEFORE the 10-K and the successor is an internal CFO with multi-year tenure - this is orderly governance, not crisis. However, the CTO departure 2 days BEFORE the CEO announcement (same week as 10-K) is unusual; CTO departures around tech-platform transitions for a fintech are non-trivial (the company is mid-migration to a new RAC POS system completed Q3 2024 and integrating Brigit technology stack). The CEO change just before a major M&A integration (Brigit) and amid negative RAC SSS deserves moderate weight. Auditor EY unchanged since 2019 (no rotation signal).

rfm_tuples.R: 'The Term Loan Facility, which matures on February 17, 2028, amortizes in equal quarterly installments at a rate of 1.00% per annum of the original principal amount thereof, with the remaining balance due at final maturity... The total interest rate on the Term Loan Facility was 7.34% at December 31, 2024.' Senior Notes $450M 6.375% due Feb 15, 2029. ABL Credit Facility matures June 7, 2029. (10-K, Note K/L)
rfm_tuples.f: Capital structure / refinancing wall: locate the largest maturity relative to the 2025-05-15 cutoff. Test whether refinancing risk is acknowledged in the 12-month liquidity framing.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Debt wall by maturity: 2025 $0, 2026 $0, 2027 $0, 2028 $802M (Term Loan), 2029 $525M ($450M Notes + $75M Q1 2025 ABL outstanding pre-Brigit). Q1 2025 10-Q discloses ABL balance ballooned to support Brigit. Term Loan SOFR + 2.75% = 7.34%; Senior Notes fixed 6.375%; ABL 6.41%. Total interest expense FY24 $107.5M (consumed 103% of OCF $104.7M). Q1 2025 interest expense $27.1M (annualized ~$108M) vs OCF run-rate ~$550M = much improved coverage.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The $802M Term Loan matures Feb 2028, just under 3 years from the cutoff. This is not an immediate refinancing wall but is material given Brigit-elevated leverage ($1.5B total at Q1 vs $1.3B FY24-end). FY24 interest expense exceeded operating cash flow (103% coverage) - though Q1 2025 OCF rebound resolves this. The 'sufficient for next 12 months' framing is honest but the 2028 wall under deteriorating RAC trajectory and pending state-AG litigation deserves vigilance. Net leverage manageable (~2.7x FY24 EBITDA) but not low for a securitized subprime LTO.

rfm_tuples.R: 'According to data released by the Fair Isaac Corporation on October 29, 2024, consumers in the subprime category (those with credit scores below 650) made up approximately 25% of the United States population. Approximately 31% of U.S. consumers have incomes below $50,000 and may lack access to traditional credit. The lease-to-own industry provides customers the opportunity to obtain merchandise they might otherwise be unable to obtain due to insufficient cash resources or a lack of access to credit to finance a purchase.' (10-K, Industry & Competition)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B customer-concentration check: UPBD entire customer base is subprime/credit-constrained households - among the most macro-sensitive cohorts. Test sensitivity to current macro: tariff impact, real wage trajectory, tax refund timing.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 100% of LTO customer base by definition is subprime. Q1 2025 10-Q adds new risk language on 'changes in tariff policies' (added since FY24 10-K). Q1 same-store sales DECLINED 2.0% YoY at RAC, attributed in part to underwriting tightening. Acima LCO improving to 8.9% (vs 9.6% Q1 2024) shows tighter underwriting working but at cost of revenue growth in RAC. Brigit adds 1.23M paying users at lower income tier (EWA/financial health) - directionally similar customer cohort.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The entire UPBD customer base is the most macro-sensitive cohort (subprime, sub-$50K HHI). The 10-K acknowledges this but does not stress-test for tariff pass-through or 2025 real-wage outcomes. Q1 RAC SSS turning negative confirms early macro stress on this consumer. Brigit acquisition arguably DEEPENS rather than diversifies the customer concentration to credit-constrained households. The added 'tariff policies' language in the Q1 10-Q is a Mode-B tell that management sees the macro risk increasing.

supplemental_signals.acima_segment_strength: Q1 2025 Acima revenue +13.5% YoY ($637.3M vs $561.3M); operating profit +42% YoY ($73.7M vs $51.9M); LCO rate IMPROVING (9.6% -> 8.9%). The growth engine continues to deliver verifiable numbers.

supplemental_signals.claim_evolution_summary: FY24 10-K narrative pillars survived Q1 follow-up with TWO POSITIVE deltas (CFPB dismissal, Acima accelerating) and ONE NEGATIVE delta (RAC SSS turning -2.0%). No covenant amendments, no going concern, no auditor rotation, no insider-vs-calendar mismatch.

summary: UPBD is a control_survivor name where the honesty-alpha framework correctly identifies the company as broadly transparent and well-governed despite a high regulatory/subprime risk profile. The single most important Mode-B finding is a POSITIVE one: the CFPB voluntarily dismissed-with-prejudice its lawsuit against Acima on March 6, 2025 (9 days after the 10-K was signed), releasing the $45M escrow and removing the largest existential overhang the 10-K disclosed conservatively. The Acima growth engine delivered in Q1 (13.5% revenue growth, 42% operating profit growth, LCO improvement); Brigit closed on schedule and is profitable from day one (27.7% operating margin). The genuine concerns are (1) RAC same-store sales inflected from +1.5% FY24 to -2.0% Q1 2025 indicating subprime household stress, (2) Multistate AG + NYAG litigation remain unsettled with reserves doubling and no acquisition-escrow cushion remaining, (3) post-Brigit leverage at $1.5B with Term Loan maturity in Feb 2028. Capital allocation is disciplined (zero FY24 buybacks preserved liquidity for Brigit cash close), CEO succession orderly with internal long-tenure CFO. Auditor EY unchanged since 2019, unqualified opinion, no going concern, no covenant issues. Verdict: NEUTRAL leaning LONG-tier - the framework correctly distinguishes this from a JACK-style distressed-disclosure pattern.
